The framework is explicitly voluntary and not a compliance mechanism; it is intended to be used alongside existing laws, regulations, and mandatory guidance. Developed under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-283). Framework covers all sectors, organization sizes, and AI maturity levels.","confidence":0.92}

Approaches and metrics for quantitative or qualitative measurement of the enumerated risks... are identified and selected for implementation.","source_section":"Page 20"}]},{"label":"pre_deployment_testing","confidence":0.75,"evidence":[{"quote":"Practical approaches for AI safety often relate to rigorous simulation and in-domain testing, real-time monitoring, and the ability to quickly shut down or modify misbehaving systems.","source_section":"Page 15"},{"quote":"deploying the system in production environments subject to increased testing or other controls","source_section":"Page 20"}]},{"label":"transparency_disclosure","confidence":0.85,"evidence":[{"quote":"Transparency reflects the extent to which information is available to a user when interacting with an AI system. Its scope spans from design decisions and training data to model training, the structure of the model, its intended use case","source_section":"Page 16"}]},{"label":"model_documentation","confidence":0.75,"evidence":[{"quote":"Explainable systems can be more easily debugged and monitored, and lend themselves to more thorough documentation, audit, and governance.","source_section":"Page 14"}]},{"label":"human_oversight","confidence":0.8,"evidence":[{"quote":"input from a broad and diverse set of stakeholders is required throughout the AI lifecycle to ensure that risks arising in social contexts are managed appropriately","source_section":"Page 13"},{"quote":"Individual human operators and their organizations should be answerable and held accountable for the outcomes of AI systems","source_section":"Page 15"}]}],"enforcement_mechanisms":[{"label":"soft_enforcement","confidence":0.95,"evidence":[{"quote":"This voluntary framework provides a flexible, structured, and measurable process to address AI risks throughout the AI lifecycle","source_section":"Page 4"},{"quote":"It is important to note that the AI RMF is neither a checklist nor should be used in any way to certify an AI system.","source_section":"Page 4"}]},{"label":"none_specified","confidence":0.9,"evidence":[{"quote":"using the AI RMF does not substitute for due diligence and judgment by organizations and individuals in deciding whether to design, develop, and deploy AI technologies","source_section":"Page 4"}]}]}
